newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Southeast plans T$7.5 bln cement plant.
newsitem.headline: Southeast plans T$7.5 bln cement plant.

text.p: Southeast Cement Corp said it planned to invest T$7.5 billion to build a cement plant in Taiwan's eastern Hualien county to join a government-led shift of cement production from the island's west to its east.
"We have submitted an application to the economics ministry for approval for the planned T$7.5 billion cement plant," company spokesman and vice-president Chiu Ta-lu told Reuters.
The design calls for two production lines, each with annual production capacity of 1.5 million tonnes of cement, he said. Completion is expected by 2000.
The company now can turn out 1.2 million tonnes of cement in its two plants in the southern county of Kaohsiung, Chiu said.
Southeast Cement would become the second Taiwan cement maker to invest in the east, following a huge T$80 billion cement complex by cement giant Taiwan Cement.

In late May, the economics ministry reaffirmed its commitment to end all mine exploration rights in western Taiwan by the end of 1997, a move aimed at promoting cement-making in the island's relatively underdeveloped east.
